claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy in an as-cast dendritic state.
The TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding approximately 0.5–1 wt% interstitial carbon to TiVNbTa will promote in situ TiC precipitation.
Homogenization and aging at 900–1000°C for several hours will induce a fine TiC precipitate population in carbon-modified TiVNbTa.
The resulting TiC precipitates will be nanoscale and uniformly dispersed within the BCC matrix.
Careful control of aging time can prevent excessive precipitate growth.
TiC nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation glide through precipitation strengthening.
TiC nanoprecipitates will inhibit creep mechanisms activated at elevated temperature.
Carbon addition and TiC precipitation will increase the TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K relative to 330 MPa.
The modified alloy may achieve a yield strength exceeding 500 MPa at 1273 K.
Carbon addition and TiC precipitation will increase compressive strength at 1273 K relative to the 423 MPa baseline.
The magnitude of strengthening will depend on TiC precipitate morphology and distribution.
The TiC dispersion may not remain uniform or stable at 1273 K.
The modified alloy is proposed to operate at 1273 K under compressive loading as an intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
